newsitem.title: FRANCE: First French beet test results due August 8.
newsitem.headline: First French beet test results due August 8.

text.p: The first French beet test will be carried out on August 4 or August 5, with results available on August 8, a spokeswoman for the sugar manufacturers' association SNFS said on Friday.
The association will carry out tests every two weeks until September 15.
The test measures sugar weight, the number of beets and sugar content.

In its first forecast for the 1997/98 season issued in mid-April national sugar intervention board FIRS predicted France may produce 4.20 million tonnes of beet sugar compared with 4.226 million in 1996/97.
The estimate assumed sowings would ease slightly to 420,000 hectares from 422,000 ha and the sugar yield would be 10.0 tonnes per hectare against 10.01 tonnes.
But in June FIRS said good growing conditions should allow the new crop to achieve a sugar yield of at least 10 tonnes per hectare.
The new prediction takes into account farmers' reports that rainfall in May and June helped the crop recover from a dry spell in the spring.
